chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah and Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us together from Ya'qub b. Yazid. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Umayr narrated to us from Ali b. Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Zayn al-Abidin Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said:

Among the Children of Israel was a man who would exhume graves. A neighbour of his became ill and feared death. So he sent for the exhumer and said to him: 'How was my neighbourliness toward you?' He said: 'It was the most beautiful neighbourliness.' He said: 'Then I need something from you.' He said: 'Your need is fulfilled.' He said: So he brought out two shrouds for him and said: 'I want you to take the one that is more beloved to you, so that when I am buried, you do not exhume me.'

So the exhumer refrained from that and refused to take it. So the man said to him: 'I would love for you to take it.' So he did not stop with him until he took the one that was more beloved to him. The man died, and when he was buried, the exhumer said: 'He has been buried, so how would he know whether I left his shroud or took it? I will take it.'

So he went to his grave and exhumed it, when he heard a voice screaming at him: 'Do not do it.' The exhumer was startled by that, so he left him and abandoned what he was doing. He said to his children: 'What kind of father was I to you?' They said: 'You were the best of fathers to us.' He said: 'Then I need something from you.' They said: 'Say what you wish, for we will fulfill it, God-willingly.' He said: 'When I die, I want you to take me and burn me with fire. When I become ashes, grind me, then cast me in a stormy wind — half toward the earth, and half toward the sea.' They said: 'We will do so.'

When he died, his children did what he had advised them. When they scattered him, Allah, exalted be His majesty, said to the earth: 'Gather what is in you', and said to the sea: 'Gather what is in you'. Then the man stood before Allah, exalted be His majesty. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'What caused you to advise your children to do this to you?' He said: 'By Your glory, fear of You caused me to do this.' Allah, exalted be His majesty, said: 'I will satisfy your victims, accept your fear, and forgive you.'

key_terms.بني إسرائيل: Children of Israel; the Israelites, a people frequently mentioned in Islamic scripture
key_terms.توبة: repentance; sincere turning back to God from sin
key_terms.نبّاش: grave-exhumer; one who digs up graves to steal from the dead

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the grave-exhumer among the Children of Israel who repented?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (as) narrates a story from the Children of Israel about a grave-exhumer whose dying neighbour asked him to take a shroud and not exhume his grave. The exhumer agreed but returned to the grave after burial, only to hear a supernatural voice warning him. Terrified, the exhumer repented and later asked his children to burn his body and scatter his ashes in the land and sea out of fear of God. Allah then commanded the earth and sea to reassemble him, and upon asking why he did this, the man answered it was out of fear of God. Allah accepted his fear, forgave him, and promised to satisfy his victims.
